questions.q: DO NOW Q1 — state Newton's second law as an equation.
DO NOW Q2 — give the unit of momentum.

learn.heading: LEARN 1 — Forces (should render — review is uncapped)
learn.body:
Resultant force changes motion.
Balanced forces = constant velocity.

learn.heading: LEARN 2 — F = ma
learn.body:
Force = mass x acceleration.
More force, more acceleration.

learn.heading: LEARN 3 — Momentum
learn.body:
p = m v.
Conserved in collisions.

learn.heading: LEARN 4 — Work and energy
learn.body:
Work = force x distance.
Energy is conserved.

learn.heading: LEARN 5 — Stopping distance (past the old 4-cap — should STILL render in review)
learn.body:
Thinking distance + braking distance.
Both increase with speed.

learn.heading: LEARN 6 — Terminal velocity (past the old 4-cap — should STILL render in review)
learn.body:
Weight = drag.
Resultant force zero, constant velocity.

build.question: BUILD MARK-THE-ANSWERS — Explain, using Newton's laws, why a passenger lurches forward when a car brakes sharply.
build.instruction: Mark each answer against the mark scheme. Give a level and a mark out of 6.

levelDescriptors.desc: Links inertia / Newton's first law to the passenger continuing forward and the seatbelt force.

indicativeContent.text: The passenger has inertia / tends to stay in motion (Newton's first law).
The car decelerates but the passenger keeps moving at the original speed.
So the passenger moves forward relative to the car.
A seatbelt provides the backward force to decelerate the passenger.

doesNotAward: The brakes push the passenger forward.
There is a forward force on the passenger from the car.

samples.label: Student A
samples.text: When the car brakes it pushes you forward because of the force from the brakes going into your body.
samples.comment: Misconception: there is no forward force on the passenger.

samples.label: Student B
samples.text: The passenger has inertia so by Newton's first law they keep moving forward at the same speed while the car slows down, so they move forward until the seatbelt provides a backward force.

samples.label: Student C
samples.text: They go forward because the car stops suddenly.

developing.q: APPLY DEV 1 — state the equation for weight.
APPLY DEV 2 — give the unit of force.

reaching.q: APPLY REA 1 — a 2 kg mass accelerates at 3 m/s^2. Calculate the resultant force.

mastering.q: APPLY MAS 1 — Explain, in terms of momentum, how a crumple zone reduces the force on occupants in a crash.

levelDescriptors.desc: Links change in momentum, longer time, smaller force via F = change in p / t.

indicativeContent.text: The change in momentum in the crash is fixed.
The crumple zone increases the time of the collision.
A longer time gives a smaller force.
So the force on the occupants is reduced.

doesNotAward: The crumple zone absorbs the momentum.
The crumple zone stops the force.

developing.q: REVIEW DEV — state Newton's first law.
developing.a: An object stays at rest or constant velocity unless a resultant force acts.

reaching.q: REVIEW REA — a 2 kg mass accelerates at 3 m/s^2; find the force.

mastering.q: REVIEW MAS — explain how a crumple zone reduces force using momentum.
mastering.a: Longer collision time for the same change in momentum means a smaller force (F = change in p / t).
